newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden govt seen selling Nordbanken on mkt - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sweden govt seen selling Nordbanken on mkt - paper.

text.p: The Swedish government is expected to sell half of its 59 percent stake in commercial bank Nordbanken this spring, probably by offering the shares to Swedish and foreign investors, Swedish financial newspaper Finanstidningen said on Thursday.
The second half of the stake, which in total is worth about 24 billion crowns, will probably be sold in 1998, the paper said.
The paper said that the government will most likely start selling the first half of its stake after Nordbanken releases its 1996 earnings on February 18.
"With new figures for 1996 in the open, the bank can turn to potential investors in Sweden and abroad," the paper said.
"The government will probably choose to offer shares to private persons and institutional investors in a large international offering."
The paper quoted sources as saying that the government was very unlikely to reach a secret agreement with one large buyer.

On January 3 rival Swedish business papaer Dagens Industri reported that the government was likely to sell at least part of its stake to Investor AB, the key holding company of Sweden's powerful Wallenberg family.
Such a deal would pave the way for a merger between S-E-Banken, in which the Wallenbergs hold 15 percent, and Nordbanken, Dagens Industri said.
This kind of deal was dimissed by Finanstidningen, which said it would be against the government's principles in previous privatisations, which have been to offer state shares to everyone.
The Social Democratic government would also have difficulty explaning to its supporters that it had chosen a deal with the Wallenbergs' financial empire, the paper said.
